findings.title: getClientsWithPermission never returns per-client grants and returns the literal "Clients" for an all-clients grant, which makes the role-mapping listing throw NullPointerException
findings.description:
`resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` only matches resources whose `type` column is `Clients` (`ResourceEntity` named query `findResourceIdByType`, `ResourceEntity.java:64`). Per-client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` through `resourceStore.create(...)` at `AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104`, and `JPAResourceStore.create` (`JPAResourceStore.java:62-79`) never sets a type. So a client granted a scope through its own permission is never returned.

The only resource that matches is the all-clients resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` with type `Clients` (`RepresentationToModel.java:1546` copies the type). When the scope is granted on that resource, line 140 adds its name, `"Clients"`, to the result.

The only caller, `rest/admin-ui-ext/src/main/java/org/keycloak/admin/ui/rest/AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:229-230`, passes each id to `realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream()`. `JpaRealmProvider.getClientById` returns null for `"Clients"`, so this throws NullPointerException. That caller only runs when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is also on (`AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:217`). The wrong result is in this method regardless of the caller.

findings.title: Deleting any client throws UnsupportedOperationException when both admin-fine-grained-authz flags are enabled
findings.description:
The `ClientRemovedEvent` branch runs when the V1 flag is on (`AdminPermissions.java:77`). It calls `management(...)`, which returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` when the V2 flag is also on (`AdminPermissions.java:67-68`). `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns `ClientPermissionsV2` (`MgmtPermissionsV2.java:63-68`), and its `setPermissionsEnabled` throws (`ClientPermissionsV2.java:193-195`).

`JpaRealmProvider.removeClient` publishes this event at `JpaRealmProvider.java:1006`, before the row is deleted. `DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory.publish` (`DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory.java:86-90`) does not catch exceptions, so client deletion fails whenever both flags are on. Before this change, `clients()` resolved to the V1 `ClientPermissions`, which handled this call.

The V2-only configuration avoids the throw only because the listener is gated on the V1 flag. That gate does nothing once both flags are on, and I found no rule in `Profile` that prevents enabling both.

findings.title: GET and PUT /clients/{id}/management/permissions return 500 when both admin-fine-grained-authz flags are enabled
findings.description:
`getManagementPermissions` (`ClientResource.java:706-714`) and `setManagementPermissionsEnabled` (`ClientResource.java:739-748`) are gated on the V1 flag through `requireFeature(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`. They then call `AdminPermissions.management(...)`, which is V2 when the V2 flag is also on.

Under that combination, `clients().isPermissionsEnabled` (`ClientPermissionsV2.java:188-190`), `clients().getPermissions` (`:203-205`, reached through `toMgmtRef` at `ClientResource.java:720`), `clients().resource` (`:198-200`), and `clients().setPermissionsEnabled` (`:193-195`) all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. The GET and PUT therefore return 500. Both endpoints worked before this change because `clients()` resolved to the V1 implementation.

findings.title: Cross-client token exchange throws from canExchangeTo instead of denying, so the request fails with a server error rather than ACCESS_DENIED
findings.description:
`V1TokenExchangeProvider` (enabled by `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, `V1TokenExchangeProviderFactory.java:60`) calls `AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(client, targetClient, token)` for every cross-client exchange (`AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:276`). When the V2 flag is on, `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (`ClientPermissionsV2.java:147-150`).

Before this change, the call reached the V1 implementation, which returned false, and the caller returned `ACCESS_DENIED` (`AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:277-280`). The exception is not caught at line 276, which sits outside the `try` that starts at line 287, so the client now gets a server error instead of a 403.

findings.title: hasPermission dereferences a null type resource when realm admin permissions are switched off, so client permission checks throw NullPointerException instead of returning false
findings.description:
When a client has no resource of its own, `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` loads the all-clients type resource at line 217 and passes it to `findByResource(server, resource)` at line 219. `getResourceTypeResource` returns null when `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:116-119`, `144-152`). That happens when `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()` is false (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:257-259`).

The admin-permissions client still exists in that state. `RealmAdapter.setAdminPermissionsEnabled(false)` only flips the attribute (`model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/jpa/RealmAdapter.java:1208-1210`), and `getAdminPermissionsClient()` reads only the client-id attribute (`RealmAdapter.java:1287-1292`). `JPAPolicyStore.findByResource` then dereferences `resource.getId()` (`JPAPolicyStore.java:211-215`), which throws NullPointerException.

The trigger is any per-client check by a caller with no manage or view-clients role, for example `canView(client)` → `canConfigure` → `canManage(client)`. The same shape exists in `UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission` (`UserPermissionsV2.java:117-123`), which is outside this diff.

findings.title: Clients permission resources have no display name, so the policy resources endpoint returns a null displayName for them
findings.description: `getResourceName` special-cases only Users (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:310-322`) and otherwise returns `resource.getDisplayName()` (line 325). Per-client resources are created without a display name (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:101-104`), and `ResourceAdapter.getDisplayName` returns the stored value (`model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/jpa/store/ResourceAdapter.java:76-78`). As a result, `PolicyResourceService.getResources` (`services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/admin/PolicyResourceService.java:218`) returns `displayName: null` for every Clients permission resource. The new CLIENTS type was added in this change without matching name resolution.
